tasks.title: Skills Nav Pane â€” hierarchical tree with Global / Project sections + 7 categories
tasks.description: Rework the Skills panel landed in v1.0.429 from a flat alphabetical list into a hierarchical tree. Top-level groups: Global (always shown) and {Project Name} (only when the active project has its own skills/commands/agents). Under each group, 7 collapsible category sections in this order: Project workflow, Project initiation, Code quality, Research, Codex integration, Tooling / config, Utilities. Server-side: expand discoverSkills() to scan all sources â€” user-global skills (~/.claude/skills/*/SKILL.md, currently 12), user-global commands (~/.claude/commands/*.md, currently 11), codex plugin (skills + commands + agents under ~/.claude/plugins/cache/openai-codex/codex/<ver>/, currently 11), and project-local .claude/skills/ + .claude/commands/ when a project is active. Each discovered item gets a hardcoded category mapping based on its name (kept in a const map at the top of server.js so additions are one-line edits). Discovery is memoized by directory mtime. Client-side: replace the existing flat <table> render with a tree of <details> elements (one per category, collapsed by default except first-render expansion of Project workflow). Each leaf row carries the same click-to-invoke behavior as today â€” sends /<name> to resumeTarget. Empty categories are hidden. Expected on-disk total: 34 (12 + 11 + 3 + 7 + 1). Bundled-but-not-on-disk skills like anthropic-skills:* and the built-in /init, /review, /security-review, /simplify, /update-config, /keybindings-help, /fewer-permission-prompts, /loop, /schedule, /claude-api should be added as a hardcoded supplement list once their source location is confirmed (bringing the total closer to Scott's stated 41 custom-created skills). Categorization decisions: evaluate-repo and find-skill â†’ new 'Research' category (pre-decision discovery, not code QA); flow-audit â†’ Project workflow (its output is backlog tasks); cross-boundary-audit â†’ Code quality (operates on existing code). Built this session alongside Polaris's new docs/backlog.json scaffolding flow.

tasks.title: Fix the refresh button in the backlog.
tasks.plan:
## Root Cause

The refresh button in the Backlog panel provides no visual feedback when clicked. Users cannot tell whether their refresh action is working, is still loading, or has already completed. This creates confusion and degrades the UX for an otherwise functional operation.

## Solution

Add loading feedback to the refresh button:
1. When clicked, disable the button and change its text from '?? Refresh' to '? Loadingï¿½'
2. When the server responds (success or error), re-enable the button and restore the original text
3. The feedback is minimal but gives clear signal that the action was registered and is in progress

## Implementation scope

**Files changed:**
- esources/mockup.html ï¿½ Add _onBacklogDataReceived() function, update efreshBacklogPanel() to disable button on click, hook message handlers for  acklogs-data and  acklog-error to reset button state

**No boundary changes** ï¿½ this is a pure UI-level change with no API, database, or registry impacts.

## First Proof Unit

**Expected behavior:** When a user clicks the ?? Refresh button in the Backlog panel, the button disables and shows "? Loadingï¿½". When the server responds, the button re-enables and returns to "?? Refresh".

**Verification:** Manual UI inspection in browser DevTools or visual test run.

## Dependencies

None. This task is fully isolated.

tasks.title: Add impact field to backlog items
tasks.description:
Add a three-level impact classification (minor, standard, major) to backlog tasks. This field affects workflow: minor items can skip /plan-task, major items trigger /plan-task to break work into subtasks.

## Scope

### Schema changes
- Add `impact` field to each task in docs/backlog.json with enum values: "minor", "standard" (default), "major"
- Field is optional on existing tasks; defaults to "standard" when not present

### Dashboard UI (resources/mockup.html)
- Add IMPACT column to backlog table, positioned between CATEGORY and DEPS columns
- Display impact value with visual styling (e.g., color-coding: green for minor, gray for standard, red/orange for major)
- Add impact field to both Add Task and Edit Task modals as a dropdown/select with three options
- Update edit button data attributes to pass impact value: `data-impact="{value}"`
- Update openBacklogEditModal() to accept impact parameter
- Update submitBacklogAdd() and submitBacklogEdit() to include impact in WebSocket messages

### Server (server.js)
- Update add-backlog-task message handler to include impact field when saving
- Update update-backlog-task message handler to accept and persist impact changes

### Workflow integration (future, documented only)
- **Minor items:** /plan-task documentation should note these can be skipped; users proceed directly to /start-build if preferred
- **Major items:** /plan-task guidance should instruct users to break the work into multiple subtasks, add each to backlog separately, then mark the parent major task as "production" and archive it

## Key findings from exploration

### Current backlog structure
- backlog.json tasks currently have: number, title, category, priority, status, description, plan, branch, pr_url, dependencies, proofUnits
- Status options: backlog, planned, build-started, cba-complete, cba-half-complete, build-finished, pr-reviewed, staged, smoke-tested, production, blocked, on-hold, cancelled

### UI architecture
- Backlog rendering via renderBacklogSection() at mockup.html:9086 generates table rows
- Each row has clickable status badge, edit button, and task cells for #, title, status, category, deps, priority
- Edit modal functions: openBacklogEditModal() (line 9301) accepts scope, taskNumber, title, description, priority, category
- Add modal: openBacklogAddModal() (line 9264); submitBacklogAdd() (line 9284) sends add-backlog-task WebSocket message
- Edit submit: submitBacklogEdit() (line 9314) sends update-backlog-task WebSocket message

### Styling considerations
- Existing categories use color coding: feature (green), fix/emergency fix (red), update (yellow)
- Impact can follow similar pattern or use different visual treatment (badges, icons, etc.)
- Table header styling at mockup.html:9109-9117

## Testability

1. Can add a new backlog task with impact="major"
2. Can edit existing task to set impact
3. Backlog panel displays impact value correctly for all three values
4. Add/edit modals include impact dropdown and accept all three values
5. WebSocket messages (add-backlog-task, update-backlog-task) include impact field
6. New tasks default to impact="standard" if not specified

## Dependencies

None. This is a purely additive feature with no blocking dependencies.
tasks.plan:
## Design Discussion

Current workflow forces small tasks through an unnecessarily cumbersome planning process (/plan-task), creating friction and slowing delivery. Conversely, large tasks skip planning/breakdown entirely, leading to unfocused, noisy code that's error-prone and hard to manage. The impact field enables right-sizing the process to match task complexity: lightweight tasks get a fast path, complex tasks get decomposition guidance upfront.

## Outline Plan

Five phases: (1) Schema & Server Foundation â€” update backlog.json and server.js handlers to accept impact. (2) Backlog UI â€” Modals â€” add impact dropdown to Add and Edit modals. (3) Backlog UI â€” Table Display â€” add IMPACT column with color coding. (4) Integration & Refresh â€” ensure refresh preserves impact state. (5) Verification & Testing â€” end-to-end manual smoke test.

Phase 1 must complete before Phases 2â€“3 (UI depends on server). Phases 2â€“3 can run in parallel. Phase 4 depends on 2â€“3. Phase 5 is the final gate.

Estimated effort: ~7.5 hours solo (3â€“4 hours with parallelization). Estimated complexity: Low â€” additive changes, no refactoring.

tasks.title: Move merge-to-stage responsibility from /finish-build to /promote-stage
tasks.description:
Change the task lifecycle so /finish-build no longer auto-merges the task PR into the shared stage branch. /finish-build should finish the task branch, verify the proof trail and registries, commit, push, open the PR targeting stage, record the PR URL, and then stop. The merge into stage is not a standalone loose step: it belongs inside /promote-stage, after /review-pr and /codex-review have completed cleanly or the user records an override.

Implementation notes:
1. Update ~/.claude/commands/finish-build.md so Step 6 opens the PR targeting stage but does not run gh pr merge. Rename the report language from "merged to stage" to "stage PR opened and awaiting review".
2. Update ~/.claude/commands/promote-stage.md so its first phase handles review-ready task PRs: find open task PRs targeting stage, verify Claude/Codex review evidence and proof-trail status, then merge approved task PRs into stage.
3. After /promote-stage merges reviewed task PRs into stage, it can continue with its existing stage promotion responsibilities: rollup audit, stage verification prompt, and stage -> main promotion PR flow.
4. Update /ship-task resumption logic so a task with an open stage PR but not merged to stage resumes by directing the user through /review-pr, /codex-review, then /promote-stage. It should not jump directly to production promotion language.
5. Update docs/backlog.json status semantics if needed: distinguish "review-ready" or "stage-pr-open" from "in-review" if the current status name implies already merged to stage.
6. Keep review inputs intentionally narrow: task description + plan, proof trail, registries/contracts, and PR diff. Do not include Soul/Architecture/session narrative unless needed, to reduce author-side framing bias.
7. Verification: run a dry task through /finish-build and confirm it stops with an open PR to stage and no merge commit on stage; then run /promote-stage and confirm it merges only reviewed/approved task PRs into stage before continuing the promotion workflow.

tasks.title: Add proof planning to /plan-task
tasks.description:
Update /plan-task so every task plan breaks implementation into proof units before any build session touches code. This is the planning side of the TDD/proof model: /plan-task does not execute TDD, but it must define the expected proof for each implementation-bearing step.

Implementation notes:
1. Update ~/.claude/commands/plan-task.md so Step 6 produces implementation steps as proof units, not plain build instructions.
2. For each unit, require: expected behavior, preferred proof type, exact command/check/manual path when known, expected initial failure, expected passing evidence, and waiver guidance if automated proof is not possible.
3. Expand the existing reachability/testability check so it becomes the task-tree entry gate: persona, entry path, required state, environment, dependencies, and first proof unit all confirmed before status flips to ready.
4. Save the proof-unit plan in docs/backlog.json and log it to the Obsidian task tracker so /start-build and /finish-build can verify against the same trail.
5. Verification: plan a dummy backlog task and confirm the saved plan contains proof units with entry/exit evidence expectations, not just implementation bullets.

tasks.description:
Enforce the proof model in the implementation-bearing workflow commands. /ship-task should orchestrate the gates, /start-build should block production code until the first proof unit is ready, and /finish-build should refuse to open or auto-merge a stage PR unless every proof unit has exit evidence or an explicit waiver.

Implementation notes:
1. Update ~/.claude/commands/ship-task.md Step 2 so after /start-build returns, the workflow does not merely say "write your code now." It should require the current proof unit: expected behavior, proof/check, observed failing result or waiver, then permission to implement.
2. Update ~/.claude/commands/start-build.md Step 8/10 so it loads the proof units from the plan, names the first unit, and blocks code-writing until entry evidence exists.
3. Update ~/.claude/commands/finish-build.md Step 2 or add Step 2a with a pre-finish self-review checklist: spec compliance, out-of-scope diff scan, registry freshness, test evidence for each proof unit, known risks/waivers, files changed summary.
4. Failure behavior: missing proof, stale registries, unexplained out-of-scope changes, or missing waiver keeps the task in in-progress and stops before gh pr create / gh pr merge.
5. Preserve pragmatic escape hatches: if no automated test is possible, require a written waiver plus a manual verification path rather than pretending automation exists.
6. Verification: create a controlled task branch with missing proof evidence and confirm /finish-build refuses before PR creation; then add evidence/waiver and confirm the workflow can proceed.

tasks.title: Define task-tree TDD/proof gate model
tasks.description:
Define the shared task-tree proof model that all Polaris workflow skills will use before any implementation-bearing step runs. The goal is broader than adding TDD to /start-build and /ship-task: every workflow step must require appropriate proof, while only implementation steps require the full red/green/refactor TDD loop.

Core model:
- Workflow entry gate before the task tree starts: task has a plan, dependencies are checked, testability path is known, and the first proof unit is identified.
- Proof unit shape: expected behavior -> proof before implementation -> observe failure or record explicit waiver -> implement smallest change -> observe passing proof -> proceed.
- Proof types: automated failing test, failing smoke command, failing API check, failing UI/browser check, registry diff expectation, manual verification script, review evidence, or explicit waiver that says no automated proof is possible and why.
- State behavior: if proof is missing or fails, stop the workflow and keep/revert the task to the previous valid lifecycle state instead of proceeding on inherited authority.
- Distinguish step roles: planning skills define proof; build skills execute proof; audit/review/promotion skills verify the proof trail.

Implementation notes:
1. Write the canonical definitions directly into the relevant command docs, starting with /plan-task, /start-build, /ship-task, /finish-build, /cross-boundary-audit, /review-pr, /codex-review, and /promote-stage.
2. Use consistent vocabulary: proof unit, entry evidence, exit evidence, waiver, proof trail, previous valid lifecycle state.
3. Decide where the proof trail is persisted: task plan in docs/backlog.json, Obsidian task tracker, PR body, or a combination. Prefer keeping summary evidence in backlog/Obsidian and detailed evidence in PR/session output.
4. Verification: run a dry task-tree walkthrough and confirm every step can say what proof it expects, where proof is recorded, and what happens when proof is missing.
